definitions.explanation: A Japanese festival held on March 3 to pray for the health and happiness of girls. Families display ornamental dolls and celebrate with special foods.

examples.japanese: ひな{祭|まつ}り⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{三月三日|さんがつみっか}だ。
ひな{祭|まつ}り⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ひな⟦{人形|にんぎょう}→人形：01487_ningyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{飾|かざ}った→飾る：01185_kazaru⟧。
examples.english: We displayed the hina dolls for Girls' Day.

examples.japanese: ひな{祭|まつ}り⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{終|お}わったら→終わる：00567_owaru⟧⟦すぐ→すぐ：00814_sugu⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧ひな⟦{人形|にんぎょう}→人形：01487_ningyou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{片付|かたづ}けない→片付ける：01192_katazukeru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧、⟦{嫁|よめ}→嫁：03670_yome⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}き→行く：00119_iku⟧⟦{遅|おく}れる→遅れる：00741_okureru⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{言|い}われている→言う：00515_iu⟧。
examples.english: It's said that if you don't put away the hina dolls right after Girls' Day, the girl will be late to marry.

notes:
WRITING:
Also written as {雛祭|ひなまつ}り or {雛|ひな}{祭|まつ}り. The kanji ⟦{雛|ひな}→雛：17377_hina⟧ means "chick" or "small doll."

CULTURAL NOTE:
Also known as ⟦{桃|もも}の{節句|せっく}→桃の節句：16519_momonosekku⟧ (Peach Blossom Festival). Families with daughters display a set of ornamental dolls (⟦{雛|ひな}{人形|にんぎょう}→雛人形：14830_hinaningyou⟧) representing the Emperor, Empress, and their court on a tiered platform. Traditional foods include ⟦ちらし{寿司|ずし}→ちらし寿司：10513_chirashizushi⟧, {菱餅|ひしもち} (diamond-shaped rice cakes), ひなあられ (sweet rice crackers), and {白酒|しろざけ} (sweet white sake).

SUPERSTITION:
It is widely believed that leaving the dolls out after March 3 will delay the daughter's marriage.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ひな⟦{人形|にんぎょう}→人形：01487_ningyou⟧: hina dolls
- ひな{祭|まつ}り⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{歌|うた}→歌：02179_uta⟧: the Girls' Day song
